_expect.name: Old Standard aka the Leaning Crack Boulder

az_old_standard_aka_the_leaning_crack_bo.blurb: A single well-regarded boulder on the east side of Cochise Stronghold in southern Arizona, close to the campground. It has six bouldering problems, running from an easy V1 and a V2 through three in the V4 range to one V5, so it suits climbers beyond the beginner stage. The defining feature is a long arching crack on the south face that rises to the tallest part of the block. The granite in this part of the Stronghold is patinaed and often compared to Joshua Tree, and the setting has a remote, backcountry feel.

az_the_roost.blurb: A small granite crag perched high on the north end of Little Granite Mountain, a desert climbing area inside Scottsdale's McDowell-Sonoran Preserve. It has six routes, split evenly between bolted and gear-protected lines, mostly 5.8 and 5.9 with a single 5.10. The rock is coarse desert granite that can feel a little crumbly in places, and the formation reads as an open book above a neighboring wall. Thick brush and aging fixed hardware keep traffic light, so expect quiet and inspect anything you clip. Little Granite as a whole leans traditional in character.

az_aztec_wall.blurb: A short bolted wall in the New World section of Christopher Creek Gorge, sitting just above the gully that separates two buttresses. The face is dark, steep and cut by several roof systems. Six sport routes cover a wide spread: one lower-angle warm-up around 5.8 and about 65 feet tall, a 5.10, three at 5.11 and a 5.12, so it rewards stronger climbers while still giving a gentle way to start the day. The trail in is shared with the neighboring Montezuma Buttress.

az_call_of_the_sirens_wall.blurb: A small amphitheater of bolted sport climbs in the Sheepshead area on the west side of Cochise Stronghold, southern Arizona. All six routes sit in a mellow band of 5.7 and 5.8, a few with plus grades, in a backcountry setting among granite domes. The lines are long enough that a 70 m rope is called for. The wall catches sun early, which makes it a good choice in cool weather; shade creeps across it as the day goes on, and most lines are shaded by mid-afternoon. Expect a hike of some length in along the Sheepshead trail.
